title: Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships
degree_levels: Integrated Master's (MMath, direct entry to Year 2)
program_type: University merit scholarship for international fee-status applicants, awarded on academic achievement
implementing_agency: University of Edinburgh — Registry Services, Scholarships and Student Funding Services (in conjunction with the School of Mathematics)
programme_action: University of Edinburgh undergraduate international scholarship scheme — School of Mathematics hosted programme award
description: The Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships are merit awards offered by the University of Edinburgh to applicants with International/EU fee status who are accepted for full-time admission to an undergraduate degree programme hosted in the School of Mathematics. Each scholarship is worth £5,000 and is paid directly to students in instalments as a contribution to living costs. The award is tenable for the duration of the programme of study, subject to satisfactory academic progress. It is not available to students already on programme, and it is not available for Mathematics studied as part of a degree hosted by another School within the University.

award_types: Fixed-value living-cost contribution of £5,000 per student
programme_structure.award_types_detail: The University states it is 'offering a number of scholarships for applicants demonstrating the highest levels of academic achievement', each worth £5,000 and paid directly to students in instalments as contributions to living costs.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Tenable for the duration of the programme of study subject to satisfactory academic progress. A student is deemed to have made satisfactory progress in each year if there has been a formal School decision of either 'Progress' or 'Conditional Progression', without the student needing to repeat a year. If the student does not make satisfactory progress in any one year the award terminates from that point onwards.
programme_structure.intake: Autumn entry (September) only. Applicants must have applied to the University of Edinburgh through UCAS, but do not need to have received an offer in order to begin the scholarship application process.

status_label: Closed for the 2026-entry round; 2027/28 funding not yet confirmed
status_note: The official scholarship page states 'The deadline to apply for this scholarship has now passed' and that 'Students will be notified of the outcome of their application by 23rd April 2026', which confirms the most recently completed round was for 2026 entry. As of the verification date (2026-10-03) the award is closed. The page further states: 'Funding for this award has yet to be confirmed for Academic Year 2027/28. Please continue to check this webpage for updated information.' Applicants targeting 2027/28 entry should monitor the official page; based on the 2026-entry round, the next application window would be expected to open ahead of a late-spring 2027 decision round.
verification_notes: Verified against the University of Edinburgh Scholarships and Student Funding site (Registry Services), the degree finder entry-requirements page for the eligible BSc Mathematics programme, and the Registry Services guidance on applying for a scholarship as a UCAS applicant. Award value (£5,000), payment method (direct to student, in instalments, as a contribution to living costs), tenability, renewal/progression condition, fee-status requirement, subject restriction (School of Mathematics-hosted programmes) and the merit-based selection basis are all confirmed from official pages. The number of awards is NOT published (the page says only 'a number of scholarships'), and the calendar application deadline with timezone is NOT currently published on the scholarship page (it states only that the deadline has passed). All English language figures quoted are the published requirements of the eligible BSc Mathematics programme, not a scholarship-specific threshold.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: One annual round. In the 2026-entry round the deadline had already passed and applicants were notified by 23 April 2026, so the application window closed in the first months of 2026. The calendar opening and closing dates of the window are published on the scholarship page only while the round is open.
application_deadline.application_period: Annual, single round, aligned to the September intake. Applicants must have already applied to the University of Edinburgh through UCAS before starting the scholarship application, but an admission offer is not required.
application_deadline.official_rule: Official scholarship page (accessed 2026-10-03): 'The deadline to apply for this scholarship has now passed.' Official Registry Services guidance 'Applying for a scholarship as a UCAS applicant': 'each scholarship fund will have a deadline, and the scholarship will only be available online until that date.' The scholarship page also states: 'Funding for this award has yet to be confirmed for Academic Year 2027/28.' No calendar date and no timezone for the deadline are published on the official page at the time of verification, so deadline_date is null rather than an assumed date. Third-party websites circulating a 31 March deadline are NOT official sources and have not been used.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Do not rely on third-party deadline aggregators. The University does not publish the calendar deadline for this award once a round has closed; the deadline and timezone are only visible on the scholarship page while a round is open, and 2027/28 funding is not yet confirmed. Check https://registryservices.ed.ac.uk/student-funding/undergraduate/international/mathematics and email lynsey.aitken@ed.ac.uk for the confirmed round dates.

programme_duration.official_range: Tenable for the duration of the programme of study, subject to satisfactory academic progress.
programme_duration.renewal_note: The award continues for the duration of the undergraduate programme provided that each year results in a formal School decision of 'Progress' or 'Conditional Progression' without the student repeating a year. If satisfactory progress is not made in any one year, the award terminates from that point onwards. The £5,000 figure is a single total per student paid in instalments, not a guaranteed £5,000 per year.

funding.monthly_amount_note: There is no monthly stipend. The £5,000 is paid directly to students in instalments as contributions to living costs; the official page does not state the instalment schedule, the number of instalments or a monthly amount.
funding.fully_funded_note: The award is a £5,000 contribution to living costs only. It does not cover tuition fees, travel, visas, installation or insurance, and it is not a full scholarship.

tuition.conditions: Not covered. The award is paid to students as a contribution to living costs and does not reduce tuition fees. International undergraduate tuition fees at Edinburgh are set by the University (it is an International/EU-EEA Overseas or Overseas fee rate) and are charged as a fixed annual fee for the whole programme based on the start date.

monthly_stipend.conditions: No monthly stipend or maintenance payment is published.

living_cost_contribution.conditions: Worth £5,000, paid directly to students in instalments as contributions to living costs, tenable for the duration of the programme of study subject to satisfactory academic progress. The instalment schedule is not published. Note: this is a single total per student, not £5,000 per year.

accommodation_support.note: Not published as an accommodation grant. The £5,000 is a general living-cost contribution that may be spent on living costs, but the page does not designate it for accommodation.

bond.note: No bond or service obligation is published for this award. The only continuing obligation is satisfactory academic progress.

total_estimated_value.conditions: Not published. The official page states the £5,000 per student value but does not publish the number of awards, so no aggregate programme value can be derived without inventing figures.

coverage: £5,000 living-cost contribution, paid directly to the student in instalments
Held for the duration of the undergraduate programme subject to satisfactory academic progress
coverage_limitations: No tuition fee support; the award does not reduce the international tuition fee liability.
No travel, visa, installation, insurance or family/dependant support is published.

The exact benefit structure may differ from cycle to cycle: the page states funding has yet to be confirmed for Academic Year 2027/28 and the University 'reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to amend or withdraw any of the advertised scholarships, without further notice' (that reservation is published on the related Global Talent Fund undergraduate page on the same site).
The number of awards is not published, so the odds of success cannot be estimated from official information.
The £5,000 is a total per student paid in instalments; the instalment schedule is not published, so the amount received in any single year is not stated.
eligible_applicants: Applicants of any nationality who hold, or will hold, International/EU fee status at the University of Edinburgh
Applicants accepted for full-time admission to an undergraduate degree programme hosted in the School of Mathematics
Applicants who have applied to the University of Edinburgh through UCAS (an admission offer is not required to begin the scholarship application)
New entrants only — students already on programme are not eligible
final_year_condition: Not applicable in the sense of a completed bachelor's degree — this is an entry award. The intended applicant pool is final-year secondary-school students (or applicants holding an equivalent school-leaving qualification) who are about to begin an undergraduate degree. Edinburgh requires that academic qualifications meet its published entry requirements for the chosen programme, and mathematics qualifications must have been achieved no more than two academic years prior to entry for the School of Mathematics programmes.
equivalent_degree_note: Equivalent school-leaving qualifications are accepted on the same basis as UK qualifications: Edinburgh publishes country-by-country entry requirements and states on the degree finder that international qualification requirements can be selected by country. For the eligible BSc Mathematics programme the published standard ranges are SQA Highers AAAAA (with BBB in one year of S4–S6, Mathematics at A); A levels from A*A*A* to A*AB (Mathematics at A*); IB 38 points with 766 at HL to 34 points with 765 at HL with HL Mathematics (Analysis and approaches only) at 7.

eligibility.citizenship: No nationality restriction. Open to applicants from any country, provided they hold International/EU fee status. (Note that the wider University also runs donor awards restricted to particular nationalities, and separately holds the Defne-Muhtar Kent Education Foundation Scholarship which is restricted to Turkish applicants, but those are distinct awards.)
eligibility.residence_requirement: No domicile or residence requirement is published for this award. The operative condition is fee status, which Edinburgh determines on the basis of nationality and ordinary residence, confirms only after application, and fixes for the whole programme.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Applicants must be entering a full-time undergraduate degree programme hosted in the School of Mathematics and must meet that programme's published entry requirements, including required subjects (Mathematics at the stated level). There is no prior bachelor's degree requirement.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Competitive and merit-based. The University states it is 'offering a number of scholarships for applicants demonstrating the highest levels of academic achievement' and that 'the scholarship is competitive and based on academic merit'. No numeric grade or GPA threshold is published for the scholarship itself; the relevant thresholds are the published entry requirements of the eligible programme.
eligibility.language_requirement: English language ability must be demonstrated for admission to the eligible programme. Edinburgh requires all applicants, including UK nationals, to prove English. The published requirement for the eligible BSc Mathematics programme is IELTS Academic total 6.5 with at least 5.5 in each component (see english_requirement). This is a programme admission requirement, not a separate scholarship language threshold.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: No restriction on holding another scholarship is stated on the Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships page. For context only, other University of Edinburgh awards on the same site do state that a University of Edinburgh scholarship cannot be held in combination with another University of Edinburgh scholarship, but that wording is not published for this award and should not be assumed. Confirm with the Scholarships and Student Funding Services team (scholarships@ed.ac.uk).
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Not available to students already on programme. Applicants must apply to the University through UCAS before beginning the scholarship application, but do not need an offer in hand. Scholarships are also not available to existing visiting students or applicants (per the Registry Services UCAS applicant guidance).
eligibility.field_restrictions: Restricted to undergraduate degree programmes hosted in the School of Mathematics at the University of Edinburgh. Mathematics studied as part of a degree programme hosted by another School within the University is not eligible. The School of Mathematics undergraduate portfolio comprises BSc Applied Mathematics, BSc Mathematics, BSc Mathematics and Statistics, MMath Applied Mathematics (direct entry to Year 2 only) and MMath Mathematics (direct entry to Year 2 only).

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No percentage or GPA cut-off is published for the scholarship. The University describes the award as for 'applicants demonstrating the highest levels of academic achievement' and selection as 'competitive and based on academic merit'. Any grade comparison is made through the published entry requirements of the eligible School of Mathematics programme.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: BSc Mathematics (Hons) standard entry requirements published by Edinburgh: SQA Highers AAAAA (achievement by end of S5 preferred) with BBB achieved in one year of S4–S6 and Mathematics at A (Higher Applications of Mathematics is not accepted in place of Higher Mathematics); A levels from A*A*A* to A*AB in one set of exams with Mathematics at A* (Further Mathematics preferred); IB from 38 points with 766 at HL to 34 points with 765 at HL with HL Mathematics (Analysis and approaches only) at 7. GCSE English at C or 4 is also required. Mathematics qualifications must have been achieved no more than two academic years prior to entry. International equivalents are set country by country via the Edinburgh entry-requirements finder.
selection_factors_may_include: Academic achievement as evidenced by the school qualifications used for admission
Strength and recency of mathematics qualifications
Overall competitive standing among International/EU fee-status applicants to School of Mathematics programmes
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: The scholarship page states only that the award is competitive and based on academic merit; no personal statement, leadership, community-service, portfolio or interview criterion is published for this award. (The separate Global Talent Fund BIG Scholarships on the same site do weigh collaborative spirit, leadership and financial need, but that is a different award and must not be applied to this one.)

english_requirement.minimum_ielts: IELTS Academic: total 6.5 with at least 5.5 in each component. IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted. (This is the published requirement of the eligible BSc Mathematics programme and of Edinburgh undergraduate entry generally; it is an admission requirement, not a scholarship-specific threshold.)
english_requirement.minimum_toefl: TOEFL-iBT (including Home Edition) taken before 21 January 2026: total 92 with at least 20 in each component. TOEFL-iBT (including Home Edition) taken from 21 January 2026: total 4.5 with at least 4.0 in each component. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
english_requirement.test_score_note: Figures are taken from the official entry-requirements page for the BSc Mathematics (Hons) programme at the University of Edinburgh, i.e. the programme eligible for this scholarship. English language requirements are published per programme on the Edinburgh degree finder, so the figures must be re-checked for the specific programme an applicant applies to. PTE Academic and Duolingo English Test are not listed among the accepted tests on the Edinburgh undergraduate entry-requirements pages reviewed.
accepted_tests: School/qualification routes: SQA National 5 English at C, GCSE English at C or 4, Level 2 Certificate English at C, IB Standard Level English at 5
english_requirement.minimum_c1_c2_proficiency: C1 Advanced (CAE) / C2 Proficiency (CPE): total 176 with at least 162 in each component
english_requirement.minimum_trinity_ise: ISE II with distinctions in all four components. Edinburgh states this is for 2026 entry only and that acceptance of Trinity ISE for 2027 entry is under review, with requirements to be published in early October.
english_requirement.minimum_oxford_ellt: Oxford ELLT: total 7 with at least 5 in each component. Oxford ELLT Skill Retake is not accepted.
english_requirement.minimum_oxford_test_of_english_advanced: Oxford Test of English Advanced: total 145 with at least 125 in each component.
english_requirement.school_qualifications_accepted: SQA National 5 English at C; GCSE English at C or 4; Level 2 Certificate English at C; IB Standard Level English at 5 (English ab initio is not accepted). Edinburgh also accepts other qualifications from around the world.
english_requirement.validity_note: IELTS Academic, TOEFL-iBT, Trinity ISE, Oxford ELLT and Oxford Test of English Advanced results must be no more than two years old from the start date of the programme, regardless of nationality. All other English language qualifications must be no more than three and a half years old; nationals of a majority English-speaking country or region (UKVI list) have no time limit on those other qualifications.

language_of_instruction.language_note: All undergraduate programmes in the School of Mathematics are taught in English. Applicants must demonstrate English ability for admission as set out in english_requirement.

application_method.application_route: Apply for admission to the University of Edinburgh through UCAS, then submit a separate scholarship application through the EUCLID applicant portal.
application_steps: Apply to the University of Edinburgh through UCAS for a full-time undergraduate degree programme hosted in the School of Mathematics (UCAS deadline for 2027 entry: 13 January 2027, 6:00pm GMT, for all UK, EU and international applicants; the equal-consideration deadline for medicine and veterinary medicine is 15 October 2026).
Allow the University's system checks to complete after submitting the UCAS application so that EUCLID applicant-portal access is granted.
Log in to the EUCLID applicant portal and open the 'My UG Applications' page.
Open the 'My Scholarship Applications' section and click the 'Apply for a scholarship' link.
Review the introduction screen, which links to the eligibility criteria, personal-statement guidance and how to track application progress, then click 'Begin Application'.

Select the programme of study and the Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarship (only one scholarship can be selected at a time; each programme application requires its own scholarship application if you have more than one).
Complete the automatic background eligibility checks and answer any additional eligibility questions.
Write and submit the personal statement in support of the application.
Track the decision through 'View My Scholarship Applications' and respond to the award letter if successful (review the award letter document in the 'Documents' column before accepting or declining).

selection_process.decision_maker: University of Edinburgh — School of Mathematics, with Scholarships and Student Funding Services administering the award (contact for the award: Lynsey Aitken, Student Recruitment Manager; general queries: Scholarships and Student Funding Services, scholarships@ed.ac.uk, +44 (0)131 651 4070).
possible_stages: UCAS application submitted to the University of Edinburgh
EUCLID applicant-portal access granted and scholarship application opened
Automatic background eligibility checks (fee status, programme of study)
Academic-merit review against the pool of eligible International/EU fee-status applicants
Decision issued and award letter produced in the 'Documents' column
selection_process.weighting_note: No published weighting. The official page states only that 'the scholarship is competitive and based on academic merit' and that it is for 'applicants demonstrating the highest levels of academic achievement'. No interview, portfolio or personal-statement weighting is published for this award.
selection_process.results_timing: For the 2026-entry round the University stated that students would be notified of the outcome of their application by 23 April 2026. Applicants are also notified by email when a decision has been made on a scholarship application, and can track status (pending, application incomplete, not eligible, waiting list, unsuccessful, offer outstanding) via 'View My Scholarship Applications' in EUCLID.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: No ranking or reserve-list mechanism specific to this award is published. The EUCLID guidance does define a generic 'waiting list' status meaning the application is eligible and has been placed on a reserve list.

selection_criteria.academic_excellence: Yes — the sole published criterion. The award is competitive and based on academic merit, for applicants demonstrating the highest levels of academic achievement.
selection_criteria.additional_factors: None published for this award. (Note: the separate Global Talent Fund BIG Scholarships on the same Edinburgh site also weigh collaborative spirit, leadership, aspiration to make a societal contribution and financial need — but those are published only for that award and must not be treated as criteria for this one.)

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: The scholarship funds study towards a University of Edinburgh undergraduate degree in a School of Mathematics-hosted programme; it is not itself a qualification.
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: 4 years for BSc honours programmes; 5 years for MMath integrated master's programmes, for which funding requires direct entry to Year 2 (on the related BIG award the University caps the maximum duration of funding at 4 years, but no duration cap is published for this scholarship, only tenability for the duration of the programme).
possible_awards: MMath Applied Mathematics (direct entry to Year 2 only)
MMath Mathematics (direct entry to Year 2 only)
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholarship page refers generically to 'an undergraduate degree programme hosted in the School of Mathematics' without listing programmes. The programme list above is the School of Mathematics undergraduate portfolio as published by the University on the same scholarships site and in the degree finder. Applicants must select their specific programme of study in the scholarship application form, and the automatic eligibility checks in EUCLID are tied to that programme.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Direct entry to Year 2 is possible for MMath programmes if Edinburgh has places available and requirements are met (A*A*A* in one set of exams to include Mathematics at A* and Further Mathematics at A*; or AAA in Advanced Highers to include Mathematics). Edinburgh does not publish a credit-transfer or advanced-standing policy specific to this scholarship.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Recipients remain liable for the full international tuition fee; the award does not provide a tuition reduction. International undergraduate students are charged a fixed annual fee for the whole programme based on their start date and are not affected by annual tuition-fee increases. Fee status is based on nationality and ordinary residence and is fixed for the whole programme.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Award terms are set out in the award letter, which successful applicants must review in the 'Documents' column of 'View My Scholarship Applications' before accepting or declining. The continuing condition is satisfactory academic progress (a formal School decision of 'Progress' or 'Conditional Progression' each year, without repeating a year).
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Recipients receive the same University services as all enrolled students, plus the standard Scholarships and Student Funding Services support (scholarships@ed.ac.uk, +44 (0)131 651 4070, Old College, Edinburgh EH8 9YL).

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm International/EU fee status expectation (Edinburgh confirms fee status only after application)
Apply through UCAS to a School of Mathematics-hosted undergraduate programme well before the 13 January 2027 equal-consideration deadline (6:00pm GMT)
Ensure mathematics qualifications are recent (no more than two academic years old at entry)
Meet the English language requirement (IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with at least 5.5 in each component is the published level for the eligible BSc Mathematics programme)
Wait for EUCLID applicant-portal access to be granted after the UCAS application
Draft the personal statement in advance — it is required inside the scholarship application form
Monitor the scholarship page for the opening of the round, because funding for 2027/28 is not yet confirmed
Keep the award letter and note the satisfactory-progress condition before accepting

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The personal statement is submitted inside the EUCLID scholarship application after the eligibility checks are passed, and no prompt or word limit is published on the scholarship page. Because selection is solely on academic merit for 'the highest levels of academic achievement', the statement should concentrate on demonstrated mathematical achievement and engagement (competitions, olympiads, further reading, projects, teaching or mentoring) rather than on leadership, volunteering or financial need, none of which are criteria for this award.
profile_fit_labels: High academic achiever at school level
common_mistakes: Assuming the award covers tuition — it is a £5,000 living-cost contribution only
Assuming £5,000 is paid each year — it is a single total per student paid in instalments across the programme

Applying without a UCAS application in place — scholarships are not available to applicants who have not applied for admission, and 'scholarships are not available for existing visiting students or applicants'
Applying for the wrong award — the Global Excellence Scholarship at Edinburgh is a postgraduate taught award and there is no undergraduate round of it
Applying while already enrolled — the award is not available to students already on programme
Applying for Mathematics within a degree hosted by another School — that is explicitly excluded
Writing the personal statement about leadership, volunteering or hardship, none of which are criteria for this award
Relying on third-party deadline dates (for example a 31 March date) rather than the official page, which publishes no calendar deadline while a round is closed

risk_flags.risk: Funding for Academic Year 2027/28 is explicitly not yet confirmed.
risk_flags.impact: The award may not run for 2027 entry, or may run with a different value or number of awards.
risk_flags.mitigation: Monitor https://registryservices.ed.ac.uk/student-funding/undergraduate/international/mathematics and email lynsey.aitken@ed.ac.uk. Do not build a funding plan that depends on this award.

risk_flags.risk: The number of awards is not published.
risk_flags.impact: The probability of success cannot be estimated, and applicants may over-invest effort in a single small-pot award.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the award as one of several funding options and apply in parallel to other Edinburgh and external funding. Ask the School directly for indicative numbers.

risk_flags.risk: No calendar deadline or timezone is published on the scholarship page while a round is closed.
risk_flags.impact: Applicants may miss a short window, or may rely on inaccurate third-party dates.
risk_flags.mitigation: Check the official scholarship page periodically and subscribe to University admissions updates; confirm the round dates by email before assuming a date.

risk_flags.risk: Award tenure depends on annual satisfactory academic progress and terminates if a year is repeated.
risk_flags.impact: A recipient who repeats a year or does not obtain 'Progress' or 'Conditional Progression' loses the remaining instalments mid-programme.
risk_flags.mitigation: Understand the progression rule before accepting the award letter, and plan finances so that loss of instalments would not make the programme unaffordable.

risk_flags.risk: The award is restricted to School of Mathematics-hosted programmes.
risk_flags.impact: Applicants to mathematics-adjacent degrees hosted elsewhere at Edinburgh, or to other subjects, are ineligible.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm the hosting School of the intended programme before applying; consider other Edinburgh and UK funding routes if ineligible.

risk_flags.risk: The University reserves the right to amend or withdraw advertised scholarships without notice.
risk_flags.impact: Award value, availability or terms can change after application.
risk_flags.mitigation: Verify the current terms on the official page at the point of application and read the award letter before accepting.

best_fit: A high-achieving school leaver of any nationality who will hold International/EU fee status, has applied through UCAS to a School of Mathematics-hosted undergraduate degree (BSc Applied Mathematics, BSc Mathematics, BSc Mathematics and Statistics, or MMath with direct Year 2 entry), meets the programme entry requirements including a recent Mathematics qualification and IELTS Academic 6.5 overall / 5.5 per component, and can use a £5,000 living-cost contribution towards the cost of study in Edinburgh.

Postgraduate taught applicants — the Edinburgh Global Excellence Scholarship is a postgraduate taught award and has no undergraduate round

The identical asset is also served from https://registryservices.ed.ac.uk/themes/upstream/wpp_theme/images/logo.png (HTTP 200, image/png, identical byte size), confirming it is the University's live brand asset rather than a per-page styling image. No third-party aggregator, stock or news source was used. Note: favicon.ico and apple-touch-icon.png on www.ed.ac.uk return 404, so the header logo.png is the verifiable official mark.
image.image_usage_note: No photograph was sourced. The official logo mark above is the only verified image asset. Edinburgh's ed.ac.uk pages also carry campaign banner images (for example /sites/default/files/styles/banner_768x141/public/2026-03/Edinburgh%20panorama%202026.jpg), but these are decorative site banners rather than award or provider brand assets and have not been used.

official_application_route: Apply for admission through UCAS to a School of Mathematics-hosted undergraduate programme, then submit a separate scholarship application (including a personal statement) through the 'My Scholarship Applications' section of the 'My UG Applications' page in the EUCLID applicant portal.

verification.verification_date_meaning: Date on which all official ed.ac.uk pages and assets cited in this record were read and the logo asset was retrieved and confirmed.
official_fields_confirmed: Official award name: Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships
Award value: £5,000 per student, paid directly to students in instalments as contributions to living costs
Tenability: for the duration of the programme of study, subject to satisfactory academic progress
Progression condition: formal School decision of 'Progress' or 'Conditional Progression' without repeating a year; award terminates otherwise
Eligibility: applicants with International/EU fee status accepted for full-time admission

Subject restriction: undergraduate degree programmes hosted in the School of Mathematics only; excluded if Mathematics is part of a degree hosted by another School; not available to students already on programme
Selection basis: competitive, based on academic merit, for the highest levels of academic achievement
Application prerequisite: must have applied to the University through UCAS; no offer needed to begin the scholarship application
Application route: EUCLID applicant portal, 'My UG Applications' page, 'My Scholarship Applications' section, with a personal statement
Notification timing for the most recent completed round: by 23 April 2026
Current cycle status: deadline has passed; funding not yet confirmed for Academic Year 2027/28
Contact: Lynsey Aitken, Student Recruitment Manager, lynsey.aitken@ed.ac.uk

English language requirement figures for the eligible BSc Mathematics programme (IELTS Academic 6.5/5.5, TOEFL-iBT 92/20 or 4.5/4.0, C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 176/162, Trinity ISE II distinctions, Oxford ELLT 7/5, Oxford Test of English Advanced 145/125) and test validity periods
Entry requirements for the eligible BSc Mathematics programme (SQA Highers, A levels, IB, GCSE English)
UCAS 2027 entry deadlines (13 January 2027, 6:00pm GMT equal consideration for all applicants; 15 October 2026 for medicine and veterinary medicine)
Fee-status framework: International = EU-EEA Overseas Fee Rate + Overseas Fee Rate, based on nationality and ordinary residence, fixed for the programme
Absence of any Edinburgh undergraduate 'Global Excellence Scholarship' round (confirmed via the undergraduate scholarship catalogue search and site search)
programme_check_required: Exact calendar deadline and timezone for the 2027/28 round (not published while the round is closed)
Number of awards offered per round (not published)
Whether the award will run at all for 2027/28 entry, and at what value

Whether University of Edinburgh scholarships may be held in combination with each other for this award

unverified_or_removed_claims: Number of awards: NOT published on the official page — the page says only 'a number of scholarships'. Set to null rather than estimated.

Deadline date and timezone: NOT published on the official scholarship page, which states only that 'the deadline to apply for this scholarship has now passed'. deadline_date is therefore null. Third-party sites circulating a 31 March deadline for earlier rounds are not official sources and were not used.

Whether a personal scholarship application is strictly separate from admission: implied by the page ('begin the scholarship application process') and confirmed by the Registry Services EUCLID guidance, but the scholarship page itself does not state 'you must submit a separate application'.
Scholarship-specific English language threshold: not published for this award. All English figures in this record are the admission requirements of the eligible BSc Mathematics programme.

Exact international undergraduate tuition fee per year: not obtainable — Edinburgh publishes these figures in per-programme client-side tables that did not render in the fetched pages. The official instruction is to use the 'Tuition fees for this programme' tool on the degree finder.

database_notes: TARGET SCOPE CORRECTION (not a do-not-duplicate exclusion): the assigned target described a University of Edinburgh international undergraduate scholarship scheme including a 'Global Excellence Scholarship' undergraduate round and a general 'international undergraduate scholarship' award. Research confirmed that NO Edinburgh 'Global Excellence Scholarship' undergraduate round exists — the Edinburgh Global Excellence Scholarship is a postgraduate taught scheme, and it appears nowhere in the University's undergraduate scholarship catalogue (https://www.ed.ac.uk/student-funding/search-scholarships filtered to undergraduate) or in a site search. Research also confirmed that Edinburgh offers NO university-wide undergraduate scholarship for international students: the official 'International and EU students' undergraduate funding page lists only six awards, all of which are subject-specific (School of Mathematics, Royal (Dick) School of Veterinary Studies BVM&S), donor/partner-funded (Rosedale OSSD, Defne-Muhtar Kent Education Foundation), Olympiad-gated (Global Talent Fund BIG) or applicant-group-specific (Asylum Seeker Scholarship).

NEAREST OFFICIAL MATCH RECORDED: the Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships is the University's flagship international undergraduate merit award for international applicants — the official page describes it as 'awarded to international applicants who demonstrate outstanding academic performance'. It is the closest official match to the assigned target and is recorded here. It is NOT on the DO-NOT-DUPLICATE list in research/bachelor/RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md, so no substitution for duplication was needed. The other official undergraduate international awards at Edinburgh are named in this record and remain available as separate future targets.

Sibling awards deliberately NOT recorded here (each is a distinct award and none is on the do-not-duplicate list): Global Talent Fund BIG Scholarships (tuition plus living costs plus a stipend, but gated on an IMO/IOI/IPhO/RMM/EGMO medal and restricted to the same School of Mathematics programmes, with no £ figures published); Royal (Dick) School of Veterinary Studies UK Graduate/International Scholarship (£5,000 per year, two awards, BVM&S only, deadline 31 May 2026 with no timezone published); Rosedale OSSD University of Edinburgh Scholarship (£10,000, one award, first year, launched 2026); The Defne-Muhtar Kent Education Foundation Scholarship (£25,000 per year towards tuition, up to £100,000 total, one award, restricted to Turkish nationals domiciled in Turkey — excluded by the protocol's rule that eligibility should not be locked to a single excluded region); Asylum Seeker Scholarship (two awards for 2026-2027, restricted to asylum seekers).

Do NOT confuse this award with the Edinburgh Global Excellence Scholarship, which is a postgraduate taught merit award. Two third-party scholarship-listing sites describe an 'Edinburgh Global Excellence Scholarship' of £5,000–£15,000 for international postgraduate taught students; that scheme is out of scope for a bachelor's record and no undergraduate round of it exists on ed.ac.uk.

Naming: the official page H1 is plural ('Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships') while the site navigation menu labels it 'Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Maths Scholarships'. Both variants are recorded in legacy_titles/short_title. The official body text uses the singular form ('The Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarship is awarded to...').

The £5,000 is a single total per student paid in instalments across the duration of the programme, not £5,000 per year. Third-party listings describing it as '£5,000 per year' are inaccurate against the official page and were not used.

No number of awards is published. The official wording is 'We are offering a number of scholarships for applicants demonstrating the highest levels of academic achievement'. No figure has been inferred.

The calendar application deadline and timezone are not published on the official scholarship page at the time of verification; the page states only that the deadline for the last completed round has passed. deadline_date is therefore null and deadline_precision is 'typical_window' per the schema accuracy rule. Third-party deadline dates were deliberately not used.

The scholarship page was published on 2024-07-29 and carries no 'last updated' date; the linked FAQ PDF ('Scholarships Systems FAQs for Applicants') was generated 2025-10-27, which is the most recent evidence of page revision found. This is recorded as source_last_updated.

All English language figures quoted in this record are the published admission requirements of the eligible BSc Mathematics (Hons) programme, not a scholarship-specific threshold. They must be re-checked against the specific programme an applicant applies to, and Edinburgh notes that some degrees set higher English requirements.

Trinity ISE is published for 2026 entry only; Edinburgh states acceptance for 2027 entry is under review, with requirements to be published in early October. Treat that figure as provisional for 2027 entry.

The exact international undergraduate tuition fee per year could not be verified: Edinburgh publishes tuition figures in per-programme client-side tables that did not render on fetch. The official route is the 'Tuition fees for this programme' tool on the degree finder. No fee figure has been estimated.

Fee status at Edinburgh is determined on the basis of nationality and ordinary residence and is confirmed only after application; it is fixed for the whole programme. International rate covers both the EU-EEA Overseas Fee Rate and the Overseas Fee Rate, and is set at the University's discretion rather than being government-capped.

Completeness: 12 official-source fetches were performed against ed.ac.uk domains (the scholarship page, the undergraduate international funding landing page, the sibling postgraduate and subject scholarship pages, the Registry Services UCAS scholarship application guidance, the official scholarship systems FAQ PDF, the degree finder entry-requirements page for the eligible programme, the UCAS 'when to apply' page, the tuition-fee rates policy page and the scholarship catalogue/search). One undelivered item remains: the exact international undergraduate tuition fee per year, which Edinburgh renders client-side per programme.
